title: Signal Architecture v2 — risk bulletins with patch semantics and auto-apply lifecycle
one_liner: Rebuild the signal system: separate storage, risk_score, patch flavor, auto-apply on wakeup, hub-triggers-framework, loop-close on teaching arrival.
summary: Signals in v1 are stored alongside work lugs (bytype/signal/), scored by ROI, and require manual triage at wakeup. In v2: signals are risk bulletins with their own home (WAI-Spoke/signals/), carry either a JIT patch or a lug delivery, have risk_score instead of ROI, are auto-applied at wakeup, and the framework closes the loop when the proper fix lands as a teaching.
motivation: The current model creates unnecessary friction: signals compete with real work items in score_backlog.py, require manual wakeup triage, and have no patch semantics. The v2 model makes hazard mitigation automatic and lightweight — patches apply during wakeup, users are notified but not blocked, and the loop closes when the framework delivers the fix.
acceptance_criteria: Signals live in WAI-Spoke/signals/{inbound,registry,processed}/ — not in bytype/signal/
Signal schema v2: risk_score (not roi), flavor (patch|delivery), optional patch field, target field
session-start.sh reads registry.json, applies unapplied patches, emits SIGNALS line in CONTEXT HEALTH if non-empty
Patch registry is lightweight JSON: {id, flavor, applied_at, patch_type} — no content copies
Hub has WAI-Hub/signals/incoming/ — Tender wakes framework when >= 1 signal present
Framework processes signals within ~2 tender cycles: implements fix + auto-generates teaching
When teaching arrives at spoke: patch removed from registry, teaching adopted, signal archived
Existing bytype/signal/ lugs migrated: patch→signals/inbound/, delivery→backlog lug + archived
wai-lug-schema.md updated: signals documented as separate system, not a lug type
wai-reference.md updated: signal lifecycle section added
wai-signal-capture.md updated: authoring guidance for v2 schema
scope: New storage layout: WAI-Spoke/signals/ directory tree
Signal schema v2: risk_score, flavor, patch (behavioral|file), delivery_lug, target
Patch registry: WAI-Spoke/signals/registry.json — read/write by session-start.sh
session-start.sh: auto-apply patches, SIGNALS line in CONTEXT HEALTH
score_backlog.py: exclude signals (they are not in bytype/ anymore anyway)
Hub Tender trigger: detect >= 1 signal in WAI-Hub/signals/incoming/
Teaching auto-generation: framework closes signal → generates .teaching file
Loop-close: spoke wakeup detects matching teaching → removes registry entry
Migration script: triage existing bytype/signal/ lugs
out_of_scope: File patch execution (v1 patches are behavioral only — plain language directives)
Cross-hub signal routing (single hub only in v1)
Patch conflict resolution (assume signals are non-overlapping in v1)
child_lugs: impl-signal-schema-v2 — new schema: risk_score, flavor, patch, delivery_lug, target
impl-signal-storage-v2 — new WAI-Spoke/signals/ directory tree + migration
impl-signal-wakeup-v2 — session-start.sh auto-apply + SIGNALS notify line
impl-signal-hub-trigger-v1 — Tender wakes framework on hub signals >= 1
impl-signal-teaching-autogen-v1 — framework auto-generates teaching on signal close
impl-signal-loop-close-v1 — spoke detects incoming teaching, removes registry entry

design_notes.patch_type_v1: Behavioral only in v1 — plain language directives ('if X, do Y instead of Z'). File patches deferred — more complexity, less urgency.
design_notes.risk_score_bands: 1-4=NORMAL, 5-7=HIGH, 8-10=CRITICAL. CRITICAL signals wake framework within 1 tender cycle.
design_notes.wakeup_placement: Apply patches before wai-session-init block — patches may affect how the rest of session-start.sh behaves
